_note: The size guide: frostlinenorge.no/storrelser and the Storrelser button on each garment page (build.py size_guide).
All numbers are cm with the garment lying flat, so a width is half the way round.
Zip hoodie and hoodie (2026-11-12): measured by hand by Kacper on the new stock, unwashed, the chest across the whole garment as it
lies, side rib included (Alexander asked for that; the first round that day went rib to rib and came out 6 to 7.5 cm narrow).
Hoodie L length and sleeve are the factory chart's 73 and 82: the one L measured came out 3 cm short in both, an odd garment
(Alexander, 2026-11-13). Its chest (60) stays as measured; it lines up with M and XL.
Crewneck (2026-11-12): measured by hand by Paula on the new stock; M length evened to 67.5 (it read 66, the same as S).
XXL on the three tops: no new XXL in stock to measure, so XL plus the factory chart's own step to 2XL (chest +5, length +3, sleeve +2).
Factory chart: Qianshi's ERP after the Oct 2026 bulk changes (+1 cm body, +1 cm sleeve on tops, +2 cm leg on pants),
~/ftmerch-print-workspace/stock/suppliers/china-qianshi/size-charts/2026-10-09-erp-after-cm-update; the measured hoodie and zip sit
within about 2 cm of it. The ERP calls its numbers after wash.
Bukse and shorts: measured by hand on stock 2026-10-06, where a measurement within about 1 cm of the factory spec (Qianshi ERP
2026-06-24, 2026-china-size-charts.xlsx in the folder above) kept the spec: men's waist and leg opening, shorts waist, women's
shorts leg opening. The 2026-11-12 measurements of the new pants (Paula: herre XS to L; Kacper: dame) agreed within about 1 cm on
the waists and on the dame inseam, so those stayed. Bukse herre inseam is as measured on 2026-11-12 (70, 71, 74, 76; S evened to 72,
XL and XXL on the same 2 cm step): 2 cm shorter than the lengthened factory chart, so the +2 cm leg did not show on the men's pants.
The dame 2XL waist measured 50 on one garment against 46 here; left at 46 until a second one says the same.
The pants have ribbed side panels and hand measurements go rib to rib, leaving them out, so the hip of both cuts and the women's leg
opening stay at the factory spec (the 2026-11-12 ones came out 2.5 to 5 cm under again); the women's XXL carries the spec's own step
on from XL (hip +2.5, leg opening +1).
Women's shorts leg opening is the one girth the factory gives the whole way round; halved here, to one decimal.
T-skjorte, longsleeve and singlet: Stanley/Stella's own product sheets, size for size (Alexander, 2026-11-13: "as per the stanley
stella"; nothing is pressed a size down since 2026-10-23/29): t-skjorte Creator 2.0 STTU169, longsleeve Creator 2.0 Long Sleeve
STTU199, singlet Stanley Stancer STTM961, which starts at S. The sheets: api.stanleystella.com/ProductSheet/en_US/<style>.pdf,
page 3. The russ print guide (~/ftmerch-print-workspace/size-guide/storrelsesguide.html) has the same three tables. A tank pressed
on Bella+Canvas (a one-off that asks for it, or a wearer XS) is a narrower garment than this table.
Collegejakke has no table: the factory promised one in July 2026 and never sent it.
mark: the measuring line on the product photo (img/shop/-1200.webp), points in that 1200 x 1200 picture, read off the
cut-out's outline; two points are a straight line, three bend at the middle one (a sleeve over the shoulder). at: where along
the line its letter sits (default the middle of the longest stretch), to keep it off the other lines.
A garment with two cuts (bukse, shorts) shows both side by side in one table, so a letter must mean the same
measurement in both cuts (build.py stops if not); a measurement only one cut has goes last (women's shorts' hip, D).
